title: Rafael and the Monsoon
premise: Wendell Ashgrove chases storms across the Bay of Bengal to pay down a debt owed to the Vane Syndicate, whose optimism about his survival is more dangerous than any weather. When old rival Imara Kess hires his crew for a salvage run into a forbidden monsoon corridor, they discover the wreck she wants raised holds evidence that could topple the Syndicate — and Wendell's own brother helped sink it. As the storm traps them aboard a leaking boat with a mysterious salvager named Noor, Wendell must choose between paying his debt and delivering justice. In the end, he lets the boat — and the debt — go under, surfacing alive with the evidence and a new family forged in saltwater.
about_author: B. M. Zhou is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent seven years documenting shipwrecks along the Indian Ocean rim. They write adventure fiction from a houseboat that has, so far, refused to sink.

chapters.title: The Optimist's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Aboard the rust-bucket chase vessel Tern, Wendell calculates debts while his crew runs a routine storm intercept for cash. A Syndicate collector radios a friendly reminder that interest compounds faster than weather. The beat: weary competence masking dread; Wendell keeps moving because stopping means reckoning.

chapters.title: Imara's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Old rival Imara Kess docks beside them unannounced, offering triple rate for a salvage job inside the closed monsoon corridor — coordinates Wendell recognizes as the Meridian, the wreck his brother died near. He refuses; she leaves the chart anyway. Beat: temptation wrapped in grief, the past refusing to stay sunk.

chapters.title: Crew of Small Mutinies
chapters.summary: POV Sefa, the navigator. The crew debates taking Imara's job behind Wendell's back: engineer Dov needs surgery money, deckhand Priya wants out of debt-running entirely. Sefa casts the deciding vote. Beat: loyalty fracturing along fault lines of need; everyone is already compromised before the storm arrives.

chapters.title: Into the Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. They cross the exclusion line at dawn under a bruised sky. Sonar finds the Meridian exactly where it shouldn't be — intact, sealed, recently disturbed. Someone else has been diving here. Beat: awe curdling into paranoia as the first squall bands close behind them like a door.

chapters.title: Noor
chapters.summary: POV Priya. A stranger's dive light finds them at the wreck: Noor, a lone salvager who claims the Meridian holds proof her family was murdered to bury Syndicate shipping crimes — crimes documented by Wendell's brother. Beat: the stranger's grief mirrors Wendell's own; duty and vengeance begin swapping places.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The dive goes wrong: Dov is injured, the Tern takes hull damage, and they recover a waterproof case of ledgers — including payments signed by the man who now owns Wendell's debt. Beat: revelation as vertigo; every debt Wendell owes traces back to the same crime.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Calls Collect
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A Syndicate enforcement boat finds them mid-storm, offering to forgive everything if the case goes overboard. Imara reveals she was hired to lead them here as bait. Betrayed on all sides, Wendell stalls — then rams the enforcer in a rising sea. Beat: rage becoming resolve; the running stops.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The climax storm hits full force. The Tern breaks apart; the survivors cling to the wreck of the Meridian itself through the worst night of their lives, the ledger lashed to Wendell's chest. Beat: stripped to essentials — breath, grip, trust — love against duty resolved into simple survival together.

chapters.title: Surface Tension
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Dawn: five survivors on a raft, one Syndicate patrol circling, and Wendell proposing the unthinkable — turn themselves in, publicly, with the evidence. Noor warns no court will touch the Syndicate. Wendell bets on journalists instead of judges. Beat: fragile hope; choosing justice outside the law but not outside witness.

chapters.title: After the Rain
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Rescued ashore, Wendell hands the ledgers to an investigative reporter as the Syndicate's collectors watch from a distance, suddenly cautious. His debt dies with the Tern; the story goes global within weeks. He and Noor stand at the tideline where his brother's name finally rests. Beat: quiet release — survival's price paid, and worth it.
